Subject: Discovery recap: Next steps for Private/VPC deep-dive

Hi Liz —

Thanks for the productive discovery earlier this morning. Quick recap and a concrete proposal for the next step (technical deep-dive / architecture review for a Private/VPC deployment):

What I heard
- Sensitive PHI scope; must be isolated to customer VPC or on-prem.
- Target inference latency: 100–200ms p95 for real-time triage flows; burst capacity for batch inference during off-peak windows.
- Retention: logs/token metadata retained 90 days; model inputs must be purged after 30 days by default.
- Compliance: SOC 2 + HITRUST evaluation likely in scope; need audit log access.
- Timeline: pilot within 6–8 weeks, production in Q4 if billing and procurement align.

Recommended next step
- 60–75 minute Private/VPC architecture review focused on networking, access controls, and ops runbook. Attendees: your infra lead, security, our solutions + ops engineers.

Proposed times (Pacific / convert as needed):
- Wed, Jun 2 — 09:00–10:15 PT
- Thu, Jun 3 — 13:00–14:15 PT
- Fri, Jun 4 — 08:00–09:15 PT

Please tell me which slot works best or suggest two alternatives. If helpful, list any additional attendees from your side (security, infra, procurement) so we can make sure the right Redwood people are on the call.

Attached: discovery-notes-jonas.pdf (brief notes + open questions).

Thanks,
Jonas

Hi Liz / team —

Connor here — I'll be running the networking portion and the ops/runbook section of the call. A few practical items ahead of Jun 3 that will help us make the 75 minutes actionable: 

Required pre-call artifacts (ideal to have 48 hours before meeting):
- CIDR ranges for the VPC you expect to use and whether you plan NAT/gateway access
- Any static IP allowlist you can provide for egress (if peering not desired)
- Point-of-contact for on-prem firewall team (if you plan a hybrid link)
- Preferred KMS type (cloud KMS vs. HSM) and whether key material is customer-managed

Security artifacts (for the security-focused attendees):
- A sample of your retention policy for logs and sensitive inputs
- Any third-party ISV that requires outbound access during inference (agents/telemetry)

Technical notes for the meeting
- We typically ask for 10–15 minutes at the start to validate network reachability to a staging endpoint; if you can allow a short window in your firewall rules that day it speeds validation.
- Required ports: 443 outbound (TLS), optional 9411 for tracing if you want Zipkin-style traces.

Attached: ops-runbook-template.yml (runbook skeleton) and I'll paste a short checklist below.

Runbook quick checklist:
- Responsible on-call for Redwood and SummitHealth (name + mobile)
- Escalation path and 30/60/120 minute SLAs for critical failures
- Maintenance window preferences and allowed backup windows

I'll send a calendar invite with the Zoom link and an attached agenda. If Jun 3 is locked in for you, please reply-all with the final attendee list so I can ensure we have the right team.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
